title: Auto Loans: Keeping the Relationship Discount After Autopay Ends
content:
Ending autopay on an Auto Loans account does not by itself take away the relationship discount. Whether the loan keeps that discount is established from the borrower's checking records, as set out here.

## Rule

The loan retains the relationship discount when the borrower's checking records put an account of a qualifying tier in the borrower's hands on the day the loan funded. That is so when the account's opening date is the funding date or earlier and its closing date, if it has one, falls after the funding date. What happened to the account after funding makes no difference to a discount already earned, so a closure at any later date leaves it in place; an account that only came into existence after funding cannot supply the discount. Where no account meets this description, the retained relationship discount is nil.

The records consulted are the accounts' tiers and their opening and closing dates. The loan's recorded discount list does not decide the question.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical loan funded on 12 August 2030)

| Qualifying checking account | Kept? |
|---|---|
| opened 12 August 2030, still open | yes |
| opened 3 March 2027, closing date 12 August 2030 | no, its closing date does not fall after funding |
| opened 3 March 2027, closing date 13 August 2030 | yes |
| opened 13 August 2030 | no, opened later than funding |
| none on the borrower's records | no |

Only the tiers named as qualifying for the product establish the relationship; any other tier is disregarded.
